reference: Pins the model-spec `parameters` override block (a corehydro addition to the shared spec builder, see model_spec.hpp's apply_parameter_overrides) against the real library. The block writes bounds, a fixed flag, a prior distribution, and a starting value onto the ModelParameter elements a model built; the R and Python packages expose it as model_parameter(). MaximumAPosteriori is the vehicle because it maximizes data + prior, so a replaced prior moves the fitted parameters and the objective -- an override that silently failed to apply would reproduce the flat-prior baseline instead. The three cases are the baseline (no block), a tightened Normal prior on the mean with UseDefaultFlatPriors off, and a narrowed bound on the standard deviation that binds the optimizer.

assertions.note: No `parameters` block: the model's own default priors and bounds. Every other case is read against this one.
A tight Normal(15000, 1500) prior on the mean replaces the model default, pulling the MAP estimate toward 15000 relative to the baseline.

An upper bound of 4500 on the standard deviation binds (the unconstrained fit lands at 5382), with a starting value of 4000 inside it -- the model's own default start would violate the new bound and C# rejects that outright, which is itself the check that the bound reached the optimizer.
